## End-to-end exemptions

| Requirement | Category | Reason | Covered at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| auth/OAuth sign-in | `external-dependency` | Completing a Google or GitHub sign-in means driving a third-party authorization server from the browser. Stubbing it would leave the test asserting the stub rather than the provider wiring, which is the only part this requirement is about. | — |
| auth/JWT session with user id | `no-ui` | The numeric id on the session token has no representation on screen. Every authenticated page in the e2e suite depends on it to load the right user's data, but no assertion can distinguish "the id is on the session" from "the page rendered", so a browser test would not be evidence for this requirement. | — |
| auth/Server-side auth gate | `harness-cost` | The gate is only observable from an unauthenticated request, and the whole Playwright suite runs behind one shared signed-in storage state. Exercising it needs a second project with no storage state, set up and reset independently — deliberately out of scope, since auth journeys are covered in Jest. | `src/auth/__tests__/authSession.test.ts` |
| auth/First sign-in provisions user and seeds settings | `harness-cost` | The scenario is about signing in a second time and finding existing settings untouched, which needs a sign-out and a fresh sign-in the shared authenticated context does not allow. The settings suite does assert that the signed-in user already has a seeded row to edit. | `src/repository/__tests__/userRepository.test.ts` |
| auth/Sign-up with validated credentials | `harness-cost` | Sign-up needs an unauthenticated context and creates a second user that the per-test reset (scoped to the single e2e user) would leave behind. Both are solvable, and both were ruled out with the rest of the auth journeys. | `src/actions/__tests__/authActions.test.ts` |
| auth/Forgot-password does not reveal account existence | `external-dependency` | The requirement is that a reset email is sent for a known address and silently not sent for an unknown one. Proving either half from the browser needs a mail transport to observe, which the e2e stack does not run. | — |
| auth/Reset password with a valid token | `harness-cost` | The raw token only ever reaches the user by email, so a browser test would have to read it out of the database and visit the reset link by hand — and then do it from an unauthenticated context. Left to Jest with the other auth journeys. | `src/actions/__tests__/authActions.test.ts` |
| coverage-reporting/End-to-end coverage is collected from both runtimes | `no-ui` | This capability is a Node script and a CI step, not application behaviour — the requirement is about which runtimes' profiles the report reads. There is no page to open, and its own Jest tests drive the conversion against synthetic profiles in the shapes both runtimes emit. | — |
| coverage-reporting/Collection is opt-in | `no-ui` | The switch governs how the test run itself is invoked, not anything the application renders. A browser test cannot observe whether the run that launched it was profiling, and the wiring is asserted directly against package.json and the build config. | — |
| coverage-reporting/Report paths match the repository layout | `no-ui` | A property of the generated lcov file: paths repository-relative and resolving on disk. Nothing about it reaches a page, and its Jest tests assert the normalisation and the on-disk check against fixture profiles. | — |
| coverage-reporting/Report scope matches the unit layer | `no-ui` | A filtering rule over source paths in a generated file. There is no user-facing surface, and the Jest tests assert both the inclusion of src/ and the exclusion of generated code. | — |
| coverage-reporting/An empty or partial report fails the run | `no-ui` | The requirement is that a script exits non-zero. Its outcome is a red build rather than anything rendered, and each failure mode is asserted directly by running the generator over profiles missing one runtime. | — |
| coverage-reporting/Each test layer is published under its own flag | `no-ui` | This is workflow and coverage-service configuration — which flag each upload carries and whether it carries forward. It has no runtime behaviour in the app at all, and is asserted by reading build.yml and codecov.yml. | — |
| data-load-performance/Independent reads execute concurrently | `no-ui` | A requirement about how queries are dispatched and how many connections the pool allows. Latencies overlapping rather than summing is not visible in the DOM, and timing a page load would measure the machine, not the behaviour. | — |
| data-load-performance/Connection attempts fail fast | `no-ui` | A pool configuration fact: the acquisition timeout is set. Observing it would mean making the database refuse connections mid-suite, and the outcome is an error in the server log rather than anything the browser can assert. | — |
| data-load-performance/Server request duration guards against premature termination | `no-ui` | The guard is a route-segment duration declaration read by the hosting platform. It has no runtime behaviour to drive locally — the e2e server never enforces a platform timeout. | — |
| data-load-performance/Repeated holiday lookups over a date range are cached | `no-ui` | The requirement is a call-count property of the holiday cache: each year resolved once and reused. Only instrumentation can see it; the rendered saldo is identical either way, which is the point of a cache. | — |
| data-load-performance/Per-user worklog lookups bounded by time are index-backed | `no-ui` | Which index serves a query is invisible in the DOM: the page renders identically whether the read used the index or scanned the table, which is exactly what an index is for. Observing it would need EXPLAIN against the e2e database mid-run. | `src/repository/__tests__/worklogIndex.test.ts` |
| mutation-safety/A control is visibly unavailable while its mutation runs | `harness-cost` | The disabled window lasts exactly as long as one server action, so asserting it from the browser means holding the action open — intercepting the request and releasing it by hand — for a state the user perceives as a flicker. The behaviour that matters to the user, that a second tap logs nothing, is asserted end to end; this requirement is about the affordance around it and is pinned precisely in Jest. | `src/util/__tests__/useTransitionWrapper.test.ts` |
| saldo/Running balance from begin date | `harness-cost` | The worked example fixes both the begin date and the current date, and the e2e server runs on the real clock — page.clock reaches only the browser. The rest of the capability is covered end to end by comparing two begin dates, but a single named total cannot be asserted without owning the clock. | `src/services/__tests__/index.test.tsx` |
| saldo/Worklog sum aggregation takes a list as given | `no-ui` | A contract between the aggregation and its callers, not a screen. No surface renders the raw mixed-list sum any more: the day total leaves absences out (its own requirement, covered end to end) and the mini-calendar feeds this figure to a border colour rather than showing it. A browser test could only observe one caller's chosen list, which is the opposite of what this requirement states. | — |
| saldo/Saldo calculation is timezone-independent | `unit-appropriate` | Comparing two runtime timezones needs two processes: Node caches the zone at startup. The Jest suite is parameterized by TZ instead (jest.config.mjs pins a non-UTC zone, TZ=UTC npm run test:ci runs it again), which is the only way to actually vary the input this requirement is about. | — |

## data-load-performance

| Scenario | Requirement | Hash | Covered by |

| Layout and page read the same data | Shared reads are deduplicated per request | `3e0a681b66ba` | _Exempt: React's per-request cache() only dedupes inside a real request scope. The Jest harness mocks cache() to an identity function so server modules can load under jsdom, so request-scoped memoization cannot be observed there._ |
| Distinct requests are not shared | Shared reads are deduplicated per request | `6898ce8ebaed` | _Exempt: Requires two separate request scopes to observe that memoization does not leak between them. Jest has no request boundary, and the e2e layer cannot see per-request query counts._ |

| Database is slow to accept a connection | Connection attempts fail fast | `3d86a9ae34a1` | `src/repository/__tests__/prismaPool.test.ts` — bounds how long acquiring a connection may block |

| Holiday classification is unchanged | Repeated holiday lookups over a date range are cached | `f68ba62e4a75` | `src/util/__tests__/date.test.ts` — isHoliday |
| Overlap detection on write | Per-user worklog lookups bounded by time are index-backed | `b3379931fa3a` | `src/repository/__tests__/worklogIndex.test.ts` — covers the owning user and the start instant, in that order |
| Range read for rendering | Per-user worklog lookups bounded by time are index-backed | `6d11211fae01` | `src/repository/__tests__/worklogIndex.test.ts` — covers the owning user and the start instant, in that order |
| Write cost does not grow with history | Per-user worklog lookups bounded by time are index-backed | `7249eb5b94d4` | _Exempt: Asserting that the overlap read's cost is bounded by nearby entries rather than by history size means measuring query plans or timings against a real database with a seeded long history.
